archetype.name: Fringe Contender (pass-first, turnover-prone)
archetype.definition: A .500 team whose passing game still rates in the top third, but whose giveaways and leaky secondary have dragged a 14-win roster back into the wild-card scrum, and whose starting quarterback is now hurt.

report.headline: A good passing offense undone by giveaways, now without its quarterback
report.take:
A year after going 14-3 with the league's best offense by EPA, New England is 5-5 with a 221-242 scoring line. The record is honest: the point differential implies 4.9 wins, so this is not a lucky or unlucky team, just an average one. What makes it average is the split inside it. Drake Maye's passing game still ranks 10th in EPA per dropback and the offense is 8th in yards per game. The run game ranks 23rd, and the turnover margin ranks 31st: 20 giveaways against 10 takeaways.

The wins have mostly come against the soft part of the schedule: the Jets, Dolphins, Raiders and Steelers, plus the one real statement, a 29-26 upset in Buffalo as a 7-point underdog. The losses to good teams have been ugly. Jacksonville won 35-6, Green Bay put up 45 on a day the Patriots turned it over four times, and Detroit won 35-10. The defense explains part of that. Its pass rush is genuine, sixth in sack rate and eighth in sacks, and it tackles well. Behind the rush, though, the secondary gives up explosive throws at the fourth-highest rate in the league. It also allows more EPA per target to opposing WR1s than any defense.

The numbers hide two things. The offense is better than its points, because turnovers have been killing drives that were moving. That kind of turnover rate usually drifts back toward average, and last year this group was plus-0.2 a game. Vrabel is also going for it on fourth down as often as anyone, which raises the ceiling and the variance. The catch is that the regression argument assumed Maye. He is doubtful with an ankle injury, and Vrabel has said he will miss time. The only other passer on the sheet is Tommy DeVito, and a backup quarterback behind a line missing its center is not a recipe for fewer turnovers.

The schedule turns brutal after this week. Buffalo, Minnesota, Kansas City and Denver are all on the way in, alongside two winnable division games against the Jets and Dolphins. Buffalo leads the AFC East at 8-1, so the division is out of reach, and the wild card depends on how long Maye is out. The trip to the 1-8 Chargers is the cleanest win left on the board, and close to a must-have.

strengths.title: A passing game that still works
strengths.body: Even through the turnovers, the dropback offense ranks 10th in EPA and the unit is 8th in yards per game. It peaked in October, with a 25.4 passing-EPA day against Las Vegas. This is the part of last year's top offense that carried over, but it is tied to Maye's health. With a backup, expect it to slide toward average or worse.

strengths.title: A pass rush that finishes
strengths.body: New England gets home: sixth in sack rate and eighth in total sacks, even though its overall pressure rate is only middle of the pack. It finishes the pressures it creates, which tends to hold up when a team has real edge rushers. The risk is Dre'Mont Jones, who was questionable during the Detroit game.

strengths.title: Sound run defense and tackling
strengths.body: By EPA the run defense is 11th, and the missed-tackle rate is eighth-best. Rushing yards allowed look worse, but that reflects volume more than efficiency. Detroit's 191 rushing yards was the outlier, not the pattern.

concerns.title: Giveaways are erasing the offense
concerns.body: Only one team has a worse turnover margin per game. Twenty giveaways have turned a positive-EPA offense into a coin-flip team. Last year's group was on the right side of the ledger, so some of this should regress. A backup quarterback makes that a much weaker bet.

concerns.title: Secondary bleeds explosive passes
concerns.body: The pass defense ranks 25th in EPA and gives up explosive throws at the fourth-worst rate. Deep passes against it have been among the most efficient in the league. Opposing top receivers have feasted, with the worst WR1 EPA per target in football. With cornerback Carlton Davis out with a knee injury, this is a structural flaw rather than noise.

concerns.title: No run game to lean on
concerns.body: The ground game ranks 23rd in EPA and 20th in success rate. It cannot carry an offense if the passing game drops off without Maye. The line is also down center Ben Brown and Walter Rouse, and TreVeyon Henderson is on injured reserve. That leaves Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner to do it.

trend.note: The offense peaked from Week 4 through Week 7 with four straight strong passing games. Since then it has lost by 18 to Green Bay and by 25 to Detroit, and Maye was injured in the Detroit game.

nextGame.headline: The league's worst offense, met by a backup quarterback
nextGame.body:
New England comes off its bye with two weeks of rest to visit a Chargers team that is 1-8 under Jim Harbaugh. The Book has not posted a line yet. The Chargers are last in net EPA and last in offensive EPA, and they keep running even though their run game is the league's least efficient. Their line is near the bottom in sack rate and QB hits allowed, which plays straight into the Patriots' best defensive trait. Their defense is sturdier: middle of the pack in EPA, seventh on third down, and ninth in takeaways. They have also been the unluckiest team in close games, so 1-8 overstates how bad they are, if not by much.

Availability tilts toward Los Angeles. Maye is doubtful and expected to miss time, which likely means Tommy DeVito. The Patriots are also without CB Carlton Davis, C Ben Brown and OL Walter Rouse, and TreVeyon Henderson is on IR. A.J. Brown (hamstring), LB Robert Spillane and DE Dre'Mont Jones are questionable. Justin Herbert has started every game for the Chargers. WR Ladd McConkey and DT Justin Eboigbe missed their last game, though their return estimates fall before this one, and OT Trey Pipkins remains on IR.

waysToWin.title: Pass rush against a porous line
waysToWin.body: The Patriots finish pressure at a top-six sack rate, and the Chargers' line gives up sacks at the second-highest rate in football. Sacks on early downs push a struggling offense into third-and-long. They can also produce the short fields a backup quarterback needs.

waysToWin.title: Stop the run the Chargers insist on
waysToWin.body: Los Angeles passes less than expected more than any team despite owning the league's worst run EPA. New England's run defense is solid by EPA. If it wins early downs, the Chargers are left throwing from bad spots, which they do poorly.

waysToWin.title: Lean on Stevenson, take a few deep shots
waysToWin.body: Lead backs have scored well above their norms against this defense. Its pass rush is bottom-ten in pressure rate, which buys a backup quarterback time. Deep balls against the Chargers have been among the most efficient in the league, so a couple of clean shots could decide a low-scoring game.

waysToLose.title: Backup-quarterback giveaways
waysToLose.body: The Patriots already turn it over more than almost anyone. The Chargers' defense is ninth in takeaways. A few mistakes from a backup quarterback are the likeliest way a bad offense gets short fields and stays in the game.

waysToLose.title: Herbert finds the explosive throws
waysToLose.body: The Chargers' passing game has been poor, but this secondary hands out big plays, especially to WR1s, and Davis is out. A couple of chunk completions could flip a game the Patriots are otherwise controlling.

waysToLose.title: Stalled drives against a good third-down defense
waysToLose.body: New England's run game is weak, and its line is missing two pieces. The Chargers are seventh in third-down defense. Without Maye, this could turn into a string of punts and field goals that keeps a 1-8 team close late.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Patriots' pass rush, sixth in sack rate, can feast on a line that is 31st in sack rate allowed, and how cleanly the backup quarterback protects the ball.

restOfSeason.body:
The season hinges on how long Maye is out. With him, the offense is a top-ten passing unit whose turnover rate should drift back toward average. That made 9 or 10 wins plausible even against a hard closing stretch. Without him, the passing efficiency is likely to drop and the turnover problem likely to persist. A weak run game and a secondary that gives up big plays leave little to fall back on. Buffalo, Minnesota, Kansas City and Denver are all good teams, so the realistic path runs through the Chargers, Jets and Dolphins plus one upset.

What is sustainable is the pass rush and the run defense. What should regress is the turnover margin, which is unlikely to stay this extreme, though a backup quarterback may keep it negative. Expect scoring to dip while Maye is out and the points allowed to stay in the low-to-mid 20s. The secondary is the defense's real hole, and it got thinner with Davis out.
swingFactors: Length of Drake Maye's ankle absence
Carlton Davis's return to the secondary

confidence.note: Ten games of a clear profile, but the starting quarterback's injury timeline is unknown.
